claims.status_note: author added upper and lower bound checks
claims.status_by_quote: Changed this to 1 for the lower bound and added an upper bound check.

claims.text: premature unmerged libmultiprocess subtree PR included ahead of upstream merge causes CI lint failure

claims.text: using colon as options separator conflicts with Windows filesystem paths containing drive letters

claims.text: size_t underflow and int overflow in FD accounting arithmetic bypass validation or cause assert crashes on startup

claims.text: unix socket paths containing commas cannot be reliably parsed without an escaping mechanism
claims.quote: The current implementation will accept unix:path,backup.sock=1 as valid when it should fail with Unknown socket option 'backup.sock'.

claims.status_by_quote: I changed listenAddress to update ListenAddress::address directly, so the resolved socket path is now available to both

claims.text: unformatted %d placeholders are shown literally in -help text because the description is not passed through strprintf

support.reason: IPC is a pretty generic feature, so it seems useful to be able to set different limits for different purposes (like GUIs vs mining clients).
I think this approach seems more reasonable than https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34978, even though both can work and both make sense this seems cleaner.
The -ipcbind=<address>:max-connections=8 option can later be expanded to include a whitelist of interfaces / methods (like -rpcwhitelist), unix group name and chmod flags.

Limiting IPC connections per listener makes sense. Tested manually on macOS and Linux by exercising the limit over the socket with raw and real clients, checking per-address behavior with multiple listeners, and running the new unit and functional tests.
This fixes a gap in descriptor accounting, and adds a helpful connection limiting feature, and is nicely implemented.
Still looks good! And better now with the feedback from other reviewers avoiding overflows and restoring the detailed listening log line.
Now supporting URL escaping for unambigous parsing.
Tested locally using socat/nc with max-connections=1 and 2 clients: the first one connected successfully, and the second one waited in the backlog to be accepted once the slot was freed.
Changes since last review were moving some changes to an earlier commit, adding ipc_fds constant, adding assert, updating tests and release notes.
The parsing changes look good, but the new help text has unformatted %d placeholders (comment below), so I'd re-ACK once that's fixed.
